learn: Investigate, design, prototype, test and refine.
Iterative development repeats the cycle to improve a program.
User feedback shapes each version.
lessons.try: Plan an app idea through all five stages.

learn: Pair programming: a driver types and a navigator reviews.
Diverse teams catch more problems and design better solutions.
Version control lets teams work on the same code.
lessons.try: Pair-program a small project and swap roles.

learn: Comments explain what code does and why.
Document purpose, inputs and outputs of procedures.
Credit code and ideas from others.
lessons.try: Document a program you wrote earlier.

learn: Computers store data as bits: 0 or 1.
Each binary place is a power of 2: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16...
8 bits make a byte, with 256 possible values.
lessons.try: Convert numbers 0-31 to binary.

learn: Fixed bit sizes cause overflow when numbers are too large.
Real numbers are approximated, causing rounding errors.
0.1 + 0.2 in many languages gives 0.30000000000000004.
check: Too large a number for its bits causes...
lessons.try: Test rounding errors in Python or JavaScript.

learn: Text uses codes like ASCII and Unicode.
Images are grids of pixels with RGB values.
Sound is sampled many times per second (44,100 for CD audio).
check: RGB stands for red, green and...
CD audio samples ___ times per second.
lessons.try: Encode your initials in ASCII binary.

learn: Lossless compression keeps all data (ZIP, PNG).
Lossy compression removes some data (JPEG, MP3) for smaller files.
Choose based on whether perfect quality matters.
lessons.try: Compress an image both ways and compare.

learn: Run-length encoding replaces repeats: AAAABB becomes 4A2B.
It works best for data with long runs.
Compression trades time for space.
lessons.try: Encode and decode strings with run-length encoding.

learn: Clean data by removing errors and duplicates.
Filter, sort and visualise data to find patterns.
Metadata describes data (date, location, author).
lessons.try: Analyse a public data set and present a chart.

learn: Variables store values; assignment changes them.
Expressions combine values with operators.
MOD gives the remainder: 17 MOD 5 = 2.
check: After a ← 3, a ← a + 4, a is...
lessons.try: Trace a program and record each variable's value.

learn: Lists store ordered collections.
In AP pseudocode, lists start at index 1.
Operations: append, insert, remove, length.
check: In AP pseudocode, the first index is...
lessons.try: Build a list of scores and calculate the average.

learn: FOR EACH item IN list visits every element.
Common algorithms: sum, max, min, count, filter.
Avoid index errors at list boundaries.
check: Accessing beyond the end causes an...
lessons.try: Write a procedure that finds the largest value in a list.

learn: IF/ELSE selects actions based on conditions.
AND, OR and NOT combine conditions.
Nested conditionals handle multiple cases.
lessons.try: Write a grading program using conditionals.

learn: REPEAT n TIMES and REPEAT UNTIL loop in AP pseudocode.
Loops must end; check the stop condition.
Loops process lists and repeated tasks.
check: REPEAT UNTIL stops when the condition is...
Infinite loops happen when the condition never...
lessons.try: Write a loop that counts down from 10.

learn: Procedures take parameters and may return values.
Abstraction hides details and manages complexity.
Libraries and APIs provide reusable procedures.
lessons.try: Write a procedure with two parameters and a return value.

learn: Every algorithm can be built from sequencing, selection and iteration.
Different algorithms can solve the same problem.
Algorithms can be described in pseudocode, flowcharts or code.
lessons.try: Write two different algorithms to find a list's sum.

learn: Linear search checks each item: up to n steps.
Binary search halves a sorted list each step: about log₂ n steps.
Binary search needs sorted data.
check: Binary search on 1,024 items takes at most about ___ steps.
lessons.try: Compare linear and binary search on a list of 1,000 items.

learn: Reasonable algorithms run in polynomial time; unreasonable ones grow exponentially.
Heuristics give good-enough answers when exact ones are too slow.
Some problems are undecidable: no algorithm can always solve them (the halting problem).
lessons.try: Explain why the travelling salesperson problem uses heuristics.

learn: RANDOM(a, b) gives a random integer from a to b inclusive.
Computers use pseudo-random number generators.
Randomness is used in games, simulations and security.
lessons.try: Simulate 1,000 coin flips and count heads.

learn: Simulations model real-world processes with simplifications.
They allow testing without real-world cost or danger.
Results depend on assumptions; bias can enter models.
lessons.try: Build a simple simulation of a queue at a shop.

learn: Repeated random trials estimate probabilities.
More trials give better estimates.
Monte Carlo methods can estimate π.
lessons.try: Estimate π with random points in a square.

units.t: The Internet and How It Works

learn: The internet is a network of networks.
Protocols are agreed rules: IP, TCP, HTTP, DNS.
IPv4 addresses use 32 bits; IPv6 uses 128 bits.
check: The internet is a network of...
lessons.try: Trace the route of a packet with a traceroute tool.

learn: Data is split into packets that may travel different routes.
TCP reassembles packets and resends lost ones.
Redundancy makes the internet fault-tolerant.
lessons.try: Act out packet routing with classmates.

learn: Sequential computing does one step at a time; parallel does many at once.
Speedup is limited by the parts that must run in order.
Distributed computing uses many computers on a network.
check: A task taking 60 s sequentially and 20 s in parallel has speedup...
lessons.try: Calculate speedup for a task split across processors.

learn: Phishing, malware, ransomware and keyloggers steal data or money.
Social engineering tricks people rather than machines.
Rogue access points can intercept traffic.
lessons.try: Identify phishing signs in five sample emails.

learn: Strong passwords, multi-factor authentication and software updates.
Encryption scrambles data; public key encryption uses a public and a private key.
Antivirus software and firewalls add defence.
lessons.try: Encrypt and decrypt a message with a Caesar cipher.

learn: Personally identifiable information (PII) can identify you.
Data is collected through cookies, apps and location services.
Review privacy settings and share less.
lessons.try: Audit the data an app collects about you.

learn: Innovations have intended and unintended effects.
Social media connects people but can spread misinformation.
Weigh benefits and harms of technologies.
lessons.try: Analyse the effects of one innovation.

learn: The digital divide is unequal access to technology.
Algorithms can reflect bias in their training data.
Inclusive design and diverse testing reduce bias.
lessons.try: Research a case of algorithmic bias.

learn: Copyright protects creative work; Creative Commons and open source share it.
Crowdsourcing and citizen science use many contributors.
Ethical computing considers privacy, fairness and safety.
lessons.try: Present an ethical dilemma in computing and your position.
